subject: religious-studies
title: The Six Fundamental Propositions
welcome_lead: Walk through Fletcher's six fundamental propositions and see how love does ethics one situation at a time.
meta_desc: A-Level Religious Studies adventure on the six fundamental propositions of Situation Ethics.
final_note: The propositions translate the law of love into a method for moral living.

concepts.def: Only one thing is intrinsically good, namely love; nothing else at all.
The ruling norm of Christian decision is love; nothing else.
Love and justice are the same, for justice is love distributed, nothing else.
Love wills the neighbour's good, whether we like him or not.
Only the end justifies the means; nothing else.
Love's decisions are made situationally, not prescriptively.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The first proposition asserts that love alone is intrinsically good; all other 'goods' are extrinsic and instrumental. The second names love as the sole norm of Christian decision; rules at most serve love.

The third proposition identifies love and justice: 'justice is Christian love using its head, calculating its duties, obligations, opportunities, resources.'

Proposition 4 dissociates love from feeling: agape wills the neighbour's good regardless of affection. Proposition 5 asserts that only the end (love) justifies the means; an act intrinsically wrong in another framework may be right here.

Proposition 6 insists that love's decisions are situational, not prescriptive: each context demands a fresh discernment.

Critics like William Barclay argue that Situation Ethics can collapse into subjectivism, with 'love' rationalising any action.

Pope Pius XII condemned 'situation morality' in 1952 (anticipating Fletcher) as undermining the objectivity of moral law. Defenders reply that informed agape-love provides genuine, if context-sensitive, guidance.
